policy: Every high/critical npm-audit finding fails the gate unless its root advisory is listed here with a written justification. An entry auto-voids when the npm registry publishes any version newer than maxAcceptedVersions, when reviewBy passes, or when the registry check itself fails — all three re-open the failure immediately.

entries.title: picomatch ReDoS through single-branch repeated extglobs
entries.justification: As of 2026-11-17 every published picomatch version (latest 4.0.7, 2026-08-24) is inside the advisory range (<=4.0.7) and no patched release exists upstream (GHSA patched_versions = null; upstream fixes remain unmerged PRs #238/#246). Every path that pulls picomatch into this app is build/CLI toolchain only — expo/@expo/cli, @expo/metro*, metro-file-map, jest-worker/jest-util, react-native community-cli-plugin via tinyglobby/fdir (verified with npm ls picomatch --all); application source contains zero picomatch references, so the vulnerable code is not shipped in the runtime bundle. npm's only suggested 'fix' is a semver-major downgrade (expo 58 -> 54.0.33, react-native 0.88.1 -> 0.83.10), which reduces the security baseline rather than improving it. Downgrading or vendoring an unmerged patch would be cosmetic; a documented, self-expiring acceptance is the honest control until upstream publishes a fix.
